subject: Clarification: processing scope, subprocessor delegation, and retention (HarborTech)
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@harbortech.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@harbortech.com>, HarborTech Legal <legal@harbortech.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Processing scope and retention questions for the DPA

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the draft DPA — we've reviewed at a high level and have a few clarifying questions before we proceed with redlines. Our legal team flagged three items we want to confirm: 1) the processor/subprocessor delegation flow (can HarborTech require prior notice vs. explicit consent?), 2) retention periods for telemetry and logs vs. customer content (we typically require 1 year for logs, 7 years for customer records), and 3) whether Redwood will accept the SCCs + US Addendum language we provided.

I've attached our redline (HarborTech_DPA_redline_v1.pdf) and a short note from legal. Can you confirm the expected review owners on your side and an estimated timeline for sign-off? We are targeting the pilot launch week of Nov 8 and would need an executed DPA before then.

Appreciate it —
Aisha
Legal Counsel
HarborTech

--- attachment: HarborTech_DPA_redline_v1.pdf (pdf) ---

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@harbortech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Processing scope and retention questions for the DPA

Hi Aisha — thanks for the redline and for highlighting the timeline. Looping in Marissa (Legal Ops) and Karthik (Account) to coordinate. Quick answers up front:

- Processor/subprocessor delegation: Redwood's standard position is notification + opportunity to object for material subprocessors; for security-critical subprocessors we require prior approval. Happy to mark which vendors fall into which bucket in the matrix.
- Retention: we can accept a 1 year retention for telemetry/logs; for customer content we traditionally mirror the contractual retention you specify (we'll commit to 7 years if required but need to confirm backup/archival costs).
- SCCs: we can accept SCCs; need to sync on the US Addendum language (some boilerplate edits needed for our hosting model).

Next steps I propose: Marissa to review the attached redline and produce a concise set of requested changes (docx) vs. our proposed compromise language. I'll then send a single consolidated response and a processor matrix that maps our subprocessors and approval level. Can you confirm: 1) whether the HarborTech legal team requires explicit prior consent for all subprocessors, or only for subprocessors that process customer content? 2) point person on your side for the SCCs language?

Tentative timeline from our side: Marissa will produce the proposed redline by Wed 10/21 EOD, we'll aim to return the consolidated counter by Thu 10/22, and if both sides agree we'll use DocuSign for signature during the week of 10/25-10/29. If HarborTech needs the DPA executed earlier for the pilot, flag and we'll escalate.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
Phone: (555) 212-9981

Subject: Fwd: Processing scope and retention questions for the DPA

On Wed, Oct 21, 2027 at 09:05 AM PDT Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Aisha — thanks for the redline and for highlighting the timeline. Looping in Marissa (Legal Ops) and Karthik (Account) to coordinate. Quick answers up front: ...

Hi team — I reviewed HarborTech_DPA_redline_v1.pdf and prepared a tracked-changes doc with our proposed compromise language (attached: RWI_proposed_redline.docx). Highlights:

- Subprocessor consent: we will accept notice + objection for all subprocessors; for three named security-critical subprocessors (S3/ObjStore, logging vendor, and inference-serving partner) we request prior written approval. Proposed clause: "Redwood will notify Customer of intended additions to the list of Subprocessors and will obtain prior written approval for any Subprocessor that will have access to Customer Content beyond transient compute or for which Customer has a documented regulatory requirement."
- Retention: propose 12 months for telemetry and logs, 7 years for customer content only if HarborTech assumes any long-term archival cost. If HarborTech requires automatic 7-year retention without cost sharing, we need to route to Finance for a pricing amendment.
- SCCs + US Addendum: minor edits to the US Addendum are required to reflect our private deployment options and the specific ECCs used; request HarborTech’s in-house SCC reviewer to review the redline in the drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cHarborTechDPA

Please confirm whether HarborTech will accept the prior-approval carve for only those three subprocessors or will insist on prior approval for all. If they insist on prior approval for all, we will escalate to Legal leadership and that will likely push the timeline beyond the pilot.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Legal Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

--- attachment: RWI_proposed_redline.docx (docx) ---

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@harbortech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Processing scope and retention questions for the DPA — proposed route to signature

Aisha — thanks for the quick replies in thread. Per Marissa's review above, here's the consolidated position and proposed operational plan so we can keep to HarborTech's pilot schedule: 

1) Subprocessors: Redwood's concession: notice + objection for all subprocessors; prior written approval required for three named security-critical subprocessors (we've listed them in the attached CSV). If HarborTech requires prior approval for every subprocessor, let us know ASAP and we'll escalate — estimate +5 business days.

2) Retention: Redwood agrees to 12 months for telemetry/logs. For customer content: we will accept HarborTech's 7-year retention request provided HarborTech agrees to a pricing addendum to cover archival costs. If you prefer Redwood to absorb that cost, we will need exec signoff and a longer procurement timeline.

3) SCCs: please have your SCC reviewer look at the proposed edits in the drive link. We are comfortable with the SCCs plus a short US Addendum update.

Planned route to signature:
- Today: Marissa uploads RWI_proposed_redline.docx and processor matrix to the shared drive (link above).
- Mon 10/25: Mutual call to close any open SCC language items (Marissa + HarborTech SCC reviewer).
- Tue 10/26: Final redline uploaded, parties confirm pricing addendum terms if required.
- Wed 10/27: DocuSign packet prepared (DPA + pricing addendum if applicable).
- Thu 10/28: Target signatures.

If that timeline works, please reply with: (a) confirmation that HarborTech will accept the prior-approval carve limited to the three named vendors, or (b) explicit request for prior approval on all subprocessors (so we can escalate). Also confirm whether HarborTech will cover archival costs for the 7-year retention for customer content.

Thanks — we want to keep the pilot date intact and are aligned to be responsive this week.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
Phone: (555) 212-9981
